question: The area of a right-angled triangle is three-fourths of the area of a rhombus, whose one diagonal is 48 cm long. The sides containing the right angle of the triangle are 36 cm and 64 cm. Find the perimeter of the rhombus.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of triangle = (1/2) × 36 × 64 = 1152

Rhombus area = (4/3) × 1152 = 1536

Area of rhombus = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂ ⇒ 1536 = (1/2) × 48 × d₂

d₂ = 64

Side = √[(48/2)² + (64/2)²] = √(24² + 32²) = 40

Perimeter = 4 × 40 = 160

**∴ Answer = 160 cm**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Right triangle sides = 36 cm and 64 cm

Area of triangle = (3/4) × area of rhombus

Diagonal d₁ = 48 cm

**Formula used:**

Area of triangle = (1/2) × base × height

Area of rhombus = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

 
 
• 
• 48 d₂ 

Diagonals bisect each other at right angle

**Calculation:**

⇒ Area of triangle = (1/2) × 36 × 64 = 1152

⇒ Area of rhombus = (4/3) × 1152 = 1536

⇒ 1536 = (1/2) × 48 × d₂

⇒ d₂ = 64

⇒ Side = √[(24)² + (32)²] = √(576 + 1024) = √1600 = 40

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × 40 = 160 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 160 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rhombus

Area = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

Diagonal Property

Diagonals bisect each other at right angles

Side of Rhombus

Side = √[(d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²]

Right Triangle Area

Area = (1/2) × base × height
